A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatentLens study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across section renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM training and interpretability experiments, human validation, ablations, captioning scores, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further VLMs, Tuned Lens, corpus-size sensitivity, and training dynamics.

M1.justification: LatentLens retains contextual-embedding retrieval by cosine similarity and the existing dynamic phrase-generation variant. Section 3.2 clarifies token indexing and retrieval across different layers, already described in v1 Section 4.3; this does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Visual Genome, PixMo-Cap, and the existing captioning, spatial-prediction, and rendered-text scenarios are retained. Additional VLMs, training checkpoints, and corpus subsamples change configurations within this coverage. The newly advertised general embedding pool is not accompanied by evaluation on a new domain.

E2.justification: EmbeddingLens and LogitLens remain the principal comparators. v4 Appendix E adds a focused evaluation of Tuned Lens against LogitLens and LatentLens on four model pairs (Table 4); v1 cited Tuned Lens but did not evaluate it.

E3.justification: The stated interpretability judge changes from GPT-4o to GPT-5, and effective training batch size changes from 32 to 8. Section 4.4 adds five off-the-shelf model configurations, reaching 72B parameters. New protocols cover corpus subsampling, intermediate training checkpoints, and Tuned Lens training on 2,000 images. These reported changes do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds corpus-size sensitivity (Section 4.5), emergence of interpretability during training (Appendix D.1), and nearest-neighbor cosine-similarity distributions (Appendix G). It also extends layer-alignment analysis to six off-the-shelf VLMs. The original connector, caption-detail, spatial-task, phrase-context, and dynamic-generation analyses remain.

E5.justification: The alternate-seed ablation and human-validation reporting remain, including 1,020 annotations, Cohen's kappa of 0.68, and 84.4% agreement accuracy. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty protocol is reported. The checkpoint experiment studies training dynamics rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Main result curves and ablation values change: the ablation baseline is 71.3% in v1 Table 1 and 72.3% in v4 Table 2. Overall LatentLens/EmbeddingLens/LogitLens averages change from 72/30/23% to 68/32/24%, with a different model pool and stated judge. v4 adds substantial results for five VLMs, Tuned Lens, corpus size, and training checkpoints; these are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical training and retrieval framework remains unchanged. v4 disambiguates sequence, token, and layer indices and describes the existing Tuned Lens affine transformation and objective. It adds no new theoretical result, formal assumption, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free contextual retrieval, greater visual-token interpretability than prior lenses reveal, and the Mid-Layer Leap. Updated model counts and aggregate scores expand the supporting evidence. The abstract retains its broad majority-interpretability claim despite exceptions in the new results.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of alignment emerging first at early layers, bimodal similarities potentially separating salient content from background, and smaller corpora reducing description granularity. It discusses weaker interpretability in larger VLMs and explicitly acknowledges that causal faithfulness to downstream behavior remains unestablished, substantially expanding the applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v1 promises a package release; v4 advertises a pip package, code access, and a broader embedding pool. Section 4.1 newly reports approximately 2 GPU hours for encoding, 13 hours total indexing time, 26 GB storage, and 29 ms retrieval per image. Appendix E adds detailed Tuned Lens optimization settings. Float8 storage and reservoir sampling were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v4 adds relevant work on discrete visual tokens, text-based CLIP interpretation, and representation alignment, including Chan, Chen, Gandelsman, and Li et al., alongside references for added VLMs. These are limited extensions to the existing positioning; the main novelty argument remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained. Local changes clarify retrieval, expand the experimental roadmap and off-the-shelf discussion, and add an Impact Statement and post-rebuttal appendix narrative. Appendix headings and cross-references are updated, although some unresolved references remain.

P2.justification: Figure 5 changes from one model's three-method plot to three method panels comparing six VLMs using normalized layer depth. v4 adds corpus-size, training-dynamics, and Tuned Lens tables, plus similarity histograms and six-model alignment heatmaps. These substantially expand the quantitative displays; most existing illustrations and appendix examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical scrutiny and practical usability through the Tuned Lens comparison, corpus-size and training-dynamics analyses, broader model evaluation, and resource/access documentation. It also states the missing causal-faithfulness evidence more clearly. However, the abstract still claims majority interpretability across all studied models and layers while Section 4.4 reports only 33–35% averages for two added models. This unresolved central overstatement limits the net quality gain.
